facts.text: Westport’s origin dates to the 1890s when a one‑dollar land sale enabled the Paducah, Tennessee and Alabama Railroad to build a line that sparked the town’s founding.
The community sits at 35°53′47″N 88°19′02″W, roughly 80 miles west of Nashville and 40 miles east of the Tennessee‑Kentucky border.
Westport’s soils are deep, well‑drained silt loams formed in loess and alluvium, making the area highly fertile for row crops like cotton and soybeans.
The town’s early settlers cleared forests for farming around 1820, establishing homesteads amid abundant game, timber, and prairie‑like barrens suitable for livestock and crops.
